description: Deploy your projects from local to your production VPS.

summary.one_liner: Airo is a Go command-line tool that builds Docker images from your local machine and deploys them to a production VPS over SSH or through a container registry, configured by an airo.yaml file.
summary.what_it_does: Airo builds Docker images for projects defined in an airo.yaml file, then delivers them to a server either by copying over SSH or by pushing to a registry. The config file sets per-image options such as base image and target architecture, and per-container options such as ports, env file path, Docker networks, and SSH or registry connection details. The `airo release` command runs build, push, and deploy in one step and generates a tag suffix automatically if none is given. Other commands cover building, pushing, deploying, listing tags locally or remotely, checking status, and printing the version. Paths to the project root and config file can be overridden with flags.
use_cases: deploy a side project to a personal VPS
build and push Docker images from a laptop
ship containers to a server over SSH
manage container deploys without Kubernetes or PaaS
use a private registry for container delivery
roll out env and config changes to running containers
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> (the README leaves the URL blank)
Create an airo.yaml in your project describing images, deploy type, containers, and ssh or registry settings
notable: Single command release that builds, pushes, and deploys a Docker image
Two delivery modes: direct copy over SSH or via a Docker registry
Declarative airo.yaml config for images and containers
Remote and local tag listing for deployed versions
Config and project root can be set by flag
caveats: The README's clone command has no URL, so the exact source location must be found elsewhere
Requires Docker and SSH access to the target VPS; the README does not describe setup on the server side
Aimed at side projects on your own server; the README does not discuss scaling or multi-host deployments
